clauses.clause: Explain concepts by interpreting texts.
Learn concepts by interpreting texts.
Construct texts to demonstrate understanding of concepts and processes.

verdicts.evidence:
- Display the What Makes Day and Night notes sheet and tell students that today they will take notes on the text What Makes Day and Night.
- Direct students to the prompts at top of the page and read them aloud:
- -'What makes day?'
- -'What makes night?'
- Tell students they will use their own notes sheet to capture quick notes about the pattern of light and dark that we call day and night. Tell students that they will use these notes in the next lesson during the Science Talk protocol. Students can use pictures and words to record their notes.
- Invite students to show a thumbs-up or touch their head if they are ready to begin writing and drawing their notes.
- Distribute:
- -Prepared clipboards with the What Makes Day and Night notes sheet
- -Pencils
- -Crayons
- -Colored pencils
- Invite students to begin working.
verdicts.rationale: Students interpret the text and illustrations to learn and explain the concept of day and night, and construct their own notes (texts) to demonstrate understanding.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Explain and learn concepts and processes by interpreting and constructing texts. (I/C)

verdicts.evidence:
Ask students to assist in filling out the first column of the anchor chart. Ask: 'What is the pattern?' (light and dark on earth, which we call day and night)
-Add 'light and dark (day and night)' to the chart.
-Ask students to help fill out the second column of the anchor chart. Ask:
'What information should we record about this pattern?'
-Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group.
-As students share responses, use their ideas to complete the second column. Example: 'The earth rotates each day. When the earth faces the sun we have day; when the earth turns away from the sun we have night.'
verdicts.rationale: Students identify the main topic and related details and explain connections between ideas from the informational text, but they do not write an independent expository piece with an introduction and closure. [REJECTED: evidence missing or not found in lesson raw text]
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote NOT found in lesson raw text (possible fabrication)
